established_findings.statement: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit diverse hallucination and miscalibration failure modes (confident factual errors, tool-execution errors, omission, etc.) that are recurrent across domains and agentic pipelines.
limitations: Derived from surveys and taxonomy papers spanning multiple domains; not all failure-mode frequencies are quantified specifically for NetOps tasks.
Surveys synthesize published reports and may emphasize observed failures without uniform measurement protocols.

established_findings.statement: Operational reliability of LLM-driven NetOps/ AIOps depends heavily on the surrounding machinery (retrieval, validators, assurance contracts, sandboxing, canary/staged rollouts) rather than on the model alone.
limitations: Principles and architecture recommendations are well argued in surveys; applied-system evidence (e.g., MeshAgent) is limited in scope and may not represent large-scale production deployments.
Exact effectiveness of specific machinery (e.g., particular canary policies) varies by context and is not exhaustively quantified in the supplied records.

established_findings.statement: There exist formal, deterministic approaches for network-change validation (e.g., Relational NetKAT) that can certify post-change packet-trace properties and produce counterexamples.
limitations: Relational NetKAT is a specification/verification framework evaluated on benchmarks; integration effort and runtime characteristics for large, heterogeneous production networks require separate assessment.
Verifier expressiveness and scalability constraints depend on the properties encoded and network size.

established_findings.statement: Verifier-grounded generate–validate–repair workflows improve semantic correctness of model-generated artifacts in domain-specific generation tasks when explicit contracts and counterexamples are used.
limitations: Primary experimental evidence is from domain-specific work (e.g., StruSpec for music-program generation) and from configuration-template synthesis prototypes; transferability and absolute effect sizes for NetOps configurations remain to be established.
Repair success depends on quality of counterexamples, model repair strategy, and verifier coverage.

established_findings.statement: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and knowledge-grounding strategies consistently improve factual grounding and domain-specific accuracy compared to unguided generation in applied domains.
limitations: Improvements are task- and dataset-dependent; retrieval latency and index structure can affect operator QoE in real-time NetOps scenarios.
RAG reduces but does not eliminate hallucination; effectiveness depends on retrieval precision and freshness of the knowledge source.

established_findings.statement: Current benchmark practice and evaluation protocols have validity gaps for safety-critical agentic systems; niche and workflow-centered benchmarks are needed to expose operational failure modes.
limitations: Arguments are conceptual and based on audits/surveys; specific new benchmark designs and their empirical properties must be developed and validated for NetOps.
Calls for niche benchmarks do not prescribe a single accepted metric set for NetOps workflows.

unresolved_questions.statement: To what degree do combined LLM + deterministic network-change validators (e.g., NetKAT) generalize to diverse, production-scale NetOps tasks without excessive false positives/negatives or unacceptable latency?
limitations: Supplied records present validators and separately present LLM-assisted NetOps architectures; they do not report large-scale, integrated evaluations demonstrating generalization.
Practical trade-offs (runtime, coverage, alerting thresholds) are context-dependent and underreported in the provided literature.

unresolved_questions.statement: What are effective, decision-calibrated uncertainty-quantification and abstention policies for LLM outputs in cost-sensitive NetOps (when to auto-apply, when to escalate to humans, when to abstain)?
limitations: Calibration frameworks exist in other domains and prototypes (e.g., decision-calibrated uncertainty) but concrete NetOps-specific abstention thresholds and their operational costs/benefits are not established in the supplied records.
Operator acceptance and human-escalation workflows affect practical policy design.

unresolved_questions.statement: Which benchmark designs, metrics, and dataset collection practices best capture end-to-end agentic NetOps safety (including sandbox replayability, canary/rollback scoring, and trace quality) for comparative evaluation?
limitations: Surveys recommend workflow-centred evaluation but do not converge on a standard benchmark specification for NetOps.
Designing benchmarks that balance realism, reproducibility, and safety constraints remains an open engineering and governance task.

candidate_gaps.statement: There is a lack of published, reproducible empirical studies that integrate formal network-change verifiers (e.g., Relational NetKAT) with LLM-generated configuration proposals at production-representative scale.
limitations: Evidence shows the existence of verifiers and separate LLM-based config synthesis work; absence of explicit integrated large-scale experiments in the supplied records supports this gap but does not prove such experiments do not exist outside the supplied set.
The gap assessment is limited to the provided record collection.

candidate_gaps.statement: NetOps-specific benchmarking workloads that jointly measure retrieval-quality, tail latency, validator coverage, and rollback-aware safety scoring (for real-time operator workflows) are underdeveloped.
limitations: Quality–latency studies exist for log-template retrieval and RAG surveys detail benefits, but a unified NetOps benchmark combining these dimensions is not present in the supplied literature.
Designing such benchmarks requires access to representative operator logs and change traces that may be proprietary.

candidate_gaps.statement: Practical, decision-calibrated abstention/escalation policies (linking model confidence to concrete operator actions) remain to be validated empirically in NetOps contexts.
limitations: Calibration frameworks and a prototype system reporting abstention exist, but systematic studies quantifying operational outcomes (e.g., reduced incidents, operator burden) are not included in the supplied records.
Human factors (trust, latency tolerance) will shape practical policy effectiveness.

excluded_claims: LLMs alone are sufficient for production-ready autonomous NetOps without validators, sandboxes, or operator-in-the-loop safeguards.
There is published evidence that LLM-based NetOps systems have already achieved production-scale, operator-trustworthy autonomous change deployment across heterogeneous enterprise networks.
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) eliminates hallucination entirely in NetOps configuration synthesis.
Current benchmarks conclusively show that LLMs reach human-level performance across all NetOps tasks and failure modes.
